about: The one power scale (powers wave 1, docs/design/powers.md). A being's strength is its LEVEL, 1 to 1000, read from one number, its might, on the owner's anchors (levelCurve). Might for a person is his fighting worth in conscripts (A.V2S.shownConscripts, the number his sheet shows) squared, the Lanchester fighting strength of the band of conscripts he equals; for a beast of the release, the same from its duel worth and blood (the human fit below); for every other being its level is written in data. Inside the code a being also carries t = 10 x log10(might / 0.01), the even log scale the odds, gaps and draws use. The level alone does not settle a fight: each being has a profile of capabilities, and titles add to both.

people.about: ln(conscripts) = lnA + lnB x worth, fitted on 656 humans of seed 7 at the start (A.fightWorth against A.V2S.shownConscripts); used to put the release's beasts on the people's scale: conscripts x sqrt(blood / 100), squared

odds.about: the chance that A beats B: 1 / (1 + (mightB / mightA)^k) on the might, then the profile's matchup. k = 0.55: one of the release's fighter tiers (about 14 worth, one e-fold of conscripts, e squared of might) wins three fights in four. A fight is settled without the duel engine when the might differs by more than 10^hugeLog; within 10^closeLog it goes to the duel.

bands.d: Rats, crows, a stray cur. A nuisance, deadly only to the sick or the very young.
Most people: farmers, clerks, lords who never drilled (an average grown human stands at 20 to 30). A fox, a hedge cat.
A regular soldier (75 to 125), a hill wolf, a wild boar. One against one, either can die.
A knight (150 to 200), a bear, a pack of wolves. A village loses men to it.
The elite of a realm (200 to 250), a great cat, a troll. A lord sends hunters with spears and dogs.
The strongest of a kingdom (300 to 380 in most cases), an ordinary grown giant, a great bear, a young dragon. The heroes of the songs stand here.
The masters of the elder and great races, the great beasts of the old lore, the smaller grown dragons. A kingdom's champion dies here alone.
An average grown dragon (about 450), the giant kings, the great spirits. Only a host can stand against one.
A strong dragon (about 525), the elder wyrms, the sea monsters that sink fleets. Kingdoms make their peace with them.

The legends: each one of a kind, each with a title, the strongest beings on the continent, a threat to nations and, in the end, to the world. The Sword Saint, the strongest man alive, stands about 650; the three Primordial Archdemons 725 to 750; the Dragon King about 800, by far the strongest of all.

capabilities.d: weight, reach and the force of a blow
whether you can outrun it, and whether it can outrun you
how much of a blade it shrugs off; a light weapon barely bites
a scratch that kills a day later; a hardy body and a healer help
it chooses when to fight; only a bow or a spear thrown reaches it
wounds close as you make them; only fire, a long fight won or a killing blow ends it
charms, prayers and spells slide off it
it comes as many: one fighter is surrounded; a shield wall holds
it ambushes, finds you hiding and learns your tricks
breath, fire, frost, glamour or spells: the reach of a weapon means little
raw destruction over an area: breath, ruin, the sea risen; it falls on many at once and wins against numbers
the one-to-one art: finding the gap, outlasting a single foe blade to blade; it turns another's firepower aside in a duel

intelligence.d: Acts by instinct: hunger, the season, its ground. It hunts, flees and guards, and holds no grudge.
Plans an ambush and remembers a trap, but cannot bargain or reason with you.
Speaks, bargains, lies and holds a grudge. Its choices have reasons, and it can be talked to.
Old and deep: it plans for years, keeps its word or its hatred for generations, and weighs kingdoms.

masters.d: The eldest giant still on a throne. Three hundred years of war in his arms and shoulders.

skills.does: A blow that splits a glacier.
Three hundred years of war in his shoulders.
His people fight harder; his foes falter.

masters.d: Two centuries at the forge and the gate. Rune-steel on his back that no smith of men can scratch.

skills.does: He has never been moved a step from a gate he held.
His own steel, his own runes.
The old dwarf way: block, step, crush.

items.does: His own making; no smith of men can scratch it.
A short hammer that rings like a bell.

masters.d: Four hundred years with one sword. She has outlived every school that tried to teach men her way.

skills.does: Four hundred years with one sword.
She is never where the blow lands.
A cut that finds the gap in any guard.

items.does: Forged before the elves came west.

masters.d: Took his seat over the bodies of forty challengers. No man of the west has lasted a minute with him.

skills.does: Forty challengers, forty wins: pain does not slow him.
A two-handed blow nothing human blocks.

myth: The faiths speak of gods. No one has ever measured one, and the scale does not hold them: it stops at the legends.

levelCurve.about: log10(might) = a + b x level + c x level^2 from level 20 up (c > 0: each level multiplies the might by more than the one before, so 650 is far beyond 600); below level 20, fifteen levels to a tenfold. Fitted to the owner's anchors (2026-11-25): an average human 20-30 (might about 0.36), a regular soldier 75-125, a knight 150-200, an elite 200-250, a kingdom's strongest 300-380 (today's best Masters, might 400-1,250), an average grown dragon about 450, a strong one about 525; the legends above 600 are written in data.

races.about: Races have baseline bodies (GD.RACES and the v2 body: a giant grown is about B, a human about F) that lineage, a title had from birth and an innate gift change a great deal; the masters below are what the best of each people reach. A playable lineage system is a later wave.

power.about: A being's fighting power is its level's might times its titles' power (buffs.power), its items' power (gives.power) and its art: 2^(art / 5), where art is the sum over its fight skills of the rank's weight (D 1, C 2, B 4, A 8, S 16, the skills' power budget of master prompt 9) times level / 10. Skills stop at level 10: past it they only evolve or merge, so strength comes from rank, titles and items, never from levels past 10. A person's skills are already inside his fighting worth, so they count once. A few great beings fighting together add up nearly in a line: the sum of their powers, times 1.05 for each one past the first (they get in each other's way as much as they help); a host of many men keeps Lanchester's law (the hostOf rule: N^1.35 x a soldier). The comparison and the ranking read the power and the profile, never the level alone.
